title: Software supply-chain integration reconciliation
claim_boundary: This profile records section-level integration evidence and gaps. Its SCIR row IDs are repository identifiers, not NIST requirement identifiers, and no disposition is a compliance claim.

rows.threat_or_failure: A stolen developer credential or unverified signing key attributes an attacker-controlled revision to a trusted developer.
rows.required_connection: Bind phishing-resistant interactive access and hardware-protected signing to the exact source revision.
rows.rationale: Endpoint signing and source-platform authentication checks jointly protect attribution at the developer-to-SCM boundary.
rows.limitations: Repository fixtures do not prove that a live identity provider, hardware key fleet, or branch policy enforces these settings.

rows.threat_or_failure: A resolver, registry fallback, or incomplete review substitutes a different dependency graph or package byte sequence.
rows.required_connection: Bind the reviewed base/head graph, approved registry origin, frozen lockfile, and downloaded artifact digest.
rows.rationale: The dependency review identity and lockfile artifact identity are verified as one acquisition chain rather than independent scanner results.
rows.limitations: A correctly identified artifact can still contain malicious code; review quality and scanner coverage remain separate risks.

rows.integration_boundary: Reviewed source revision to build invocation
rows.threat_or_failure: A privileged rerun, alternate checkout, or changed build definition builds bytes from a revision other than the reviewed source.
rows.required_connection: Bind trusted-run creation, checked-out revision, versioned build definition, platform, and invocation parameters.
rows.rationale: Untrusted-PR separation and hosted-build invocation checks preserve the revision identity handed from SCM into the build platform.
rows.limitations: Live provider rules and run records remain organization-owned evidence.

rows.integration_boundary: Pipeline workload identity to deployment authority
rows.threat_or_failure: A stored cloud credential or weak federation claim lets the wrong workflow, repository, ref, or reusable workflow obtain deployment authority.
rows.required_connection: Bind exact OIDC issuer, audience, subject, repository, workflow, ref, environment, and short-lived cloud role to a separate deploy boundary.
rows.rationale: The build/deploy separation and exact federation claims connect pipeline identity to bounded deployment authority.
rows.limitations: The provider-neutral verifier does not prove a live cloud trust policy is installed.

rows.integration_boundary: Build platform identity to artifact digest and provenance
rows.threat_or_failure: Build steps forge platform identity or provenance describes different bytes or invocation parameters.
rows.required_connection: Generate provenance through the platform control plane and bind the artifact digest, build definition, invocation, and authenticated platform identity.
rows.rationale: Platform-generated authenticated provenance is the handoff record from a build invocation to exact output bytes.
rows.limitations: Repository fixtures do not establish the security of a live hosted builder or its signing service.

rows.integration_boundary: Artifact digest to published release evidence
rows.threat_or_failure: A release publishes missing, mutable, substituted, or signer-unbound provenance, SBOM, or signature evidence.
rows.required_connection: Bind provenance, SBOM, signing request, signature publication, and transparency receipt to one immutable artifact digest and release identity.
rows.rationale: Three release evidence types retain one artifact identity across generation and immutable publication.
rows.limitations: Live KMS, transparency service, repository, and SBOM platform evidence remains organization owned.

rows.integration_boundary: Published registry object to deployment admission identity
rows.threat_or_failure: A mutable tag, unauthorized registry operation, or admission bypass deploys bytes other than the reviewed release artifact.
rows.required_connection: Protect registry mutation and authorize deployment only for the exact trusted OCI manifest digest with matching authenticated provenance.
rows.rationale: Registry protection preserves the digest that admission re-verifies before workload creation or update.
rows.limitations: Provider-side registry and cluster admission configuration is not established by offline fixtures.

rows.integration_boundary: Deployment identity to runtime impact inventory
rows.threat_or_failure: GitOps drift, direct control-plane changes, or incomplete inventory severs the link between a deployed workload and its release evidence.
rows.required_connection: Preserve commit, artifact digest, SBOM observation, deployment ID, enforcement decision, and drift state as separate linked identities.
rows.rationale: Deployment and lifecycle inventory checks make the release-to-runtime handoff queryable without overwriting source or build observations.
rows.limitations: Live GitOps provider enforcement, cluster inventory, and deletion propagation remain external evidence.

rows.integration_boundary: Application security results to source revision
rows.threat_or_failure: A source revision advances without revision-bound SAST, DAST, authorization, authentication, injection, or secret findings being evaluated.
rows.required_connection: Bind application security test results and existing dependency and secret checks to the exact reviewed revision before promotion.
rows.gap_description: The application assessment source is still required before executable PSB-CODE controls can provide revision-bound evidence.
rows.rationale: Dependency and secret checks cover only part of secure-commit evaluation; application behavior testing remains explicitly planned.
rows.limitations: Planned IDs and partial evidence are not implementation or application-security coverage claims.

rows.integration_boundary: CI/CD human and control-plane identity to privileged configuration change
rows.threat_or_failure: A compromised administrator or provider control-plane session changes branch rules, environments, runners, federated trust, or signing policy outside the reviewed pipeline.
rows.required_connection: Collect current provider-side administrator identity, phishing-resistant session, approval, policy version, and audit event for each privileged configuration change.
rows.gap_description: No cross-provider adapter currently reconciles human administrator sessions and control-plane changes across SCM, CI, cloud federation, registry, and signing services.
rows.rationale: Runner authority and audit checks are partial evidence but do not establish the wider CI/CD control-plane identity chain.
rows.limitations: This gap must not be reported as clean merely because repository workflow checks pass.

rows.integration_boundary: Running artifact age and vulnerability state to rebuild decision
rows.threat_or_failure: An old but validly signed artifact remains deployed after dependencies, base images, or vulnerability intelligence make it unsafe.
rows.required_connection: Link deployed digest and SBOM inventory to update horizon, current vulnerability state, rebuild decision, and replacement deployment.
rows.rationale: PSB-GOV-005 joins current risk and runtime inventory to a bounded clean rebuild, exact replacement admission, and independent proof that the old digest is no longer active.
rows.limitations: The E3 verifier is offline; live scanner, build, registry, admission, and complete deployment-inventory adapters remain organization evidence.

rows.integration_boundary: Product-specific secure design and enterprise vulnerability management
rows.threat_or_failure: A pipeline-only review is mistaken for complete product threat modeling or enterprise vulnerability-management coverage.
rows.required_connection: Keep product design, business abuse cases, production SOC operation, and enterprise GRC assessments outside this CI/CD integration profile and assess them through their owning processes.
rows.gap_description: This boundary is intentionally excluded from the SP 800-204D integration profile rather than recorded as a CI/CD implementation gap.
rows.rationale: The profile is limited to software supply-chain security integration and must not imply complete product security coverage.
rows.limitations: Other repository controls and organization processes may address parts of this boundary independently.
